newsitem.title: UK: IPE BRENT TRADES SIDEWAYS SUPPORTS HOLDING.
newsitem.headline: IPE BRENT TRADES SIDEWAYS SUPPORTS HOLDING.

text.p: IPE crude and gas oil futures traded sideways on Monday, looking for fresh impetus with initial supports on both contracts holding, brokers said.
"Technically the downside potential today is limited so I expect the market to remain relatively stable", one said.
By 1306 GMT September Brent was five cents up at $18.53 a barrel after recovering from an early dip to $18.35. Gas oil was off 75 cents $168.75 with support coming around $168.
Tom James at Credit Lyonnais Rouse in Singapore said "With Iraq news and expectation already in the market I am now looking for the technicals to start helping this market hold support".
Floor brokers said they were looking for fresh direction from the NYMEX, while analysts remained optimistic that the uptrend for crude remains intact in the longer term.

Leslie Nicholas at GNI Research said in his daily report, "The weekly charts for both Brent and (NYMEX crude) show that the uptrends have not yet been negated. (NYMEX crude) for example can rally again today if $19.49 holds, while $19.25 is an important support level for the week as a whole".
$19.49 support is from Friday's low trade while trendline support, stemming from June 20's $18.35 low and passing through July 25's low of $18.98.
That comes in at around $19.25 today on the weekly chart.
